claims.text: Simultaneous wear and corrosion resistance is governed by formation of a refined, dual-phase surface structure that supports passivation and resists sliding deformation.
The initial AlCoCrFeNiMo-based alloy has a relatively coarse microstructure.
Adding boron to the AlCoCrFeNiMo-based alloy triggers in situ TiB2 formation.
Boron addition refines the alloy's grain structure.
Boron treatment produces uniformly dispersed TiB2 nano-precipitates.
Uniformly dispersed TiB2 nano-precipitates mechanically reinforce the surface.
The refined, precipitate-containing microstructure improves the formation and stability of a passive oxide film.
Grain refinement increases grain-boundary density and protective-film nucleation sites.
Under sliding stress, a refined near-surface structure facilitates dynamic amorphization.
Dynamic amorphization or formation of an ultra-nanocrystalline near-surface layer lowers friction and wear.
A stable passive film resists corrosive attack during sliding.
The interaction of mechanical reinforcement, dynamic amorphization, and stable passivation minimizes both physical and chemical degradation.
The boron-doped alloy will have a lower wear rate than the matched undoped baseline.
The boron-doped alloy will have a lower friction coefficient than the matched undoped baseline.
The boron-doped alloy will exhibit a more noble corrosion potential and lower corrosion current density.
Combined wear-corrosion degradation will be significantly lower in the boron-doped alloy.
The predicted benefit holds at moderate-to-high wear-corrosion severity provided passive-film formation is not completely disrupted.
The benefit may disappear in inert environments or at loads exceeding the passive film's protective capacity.

contradictions.description: The stated AlCoCrFeNiMo starting alloy contains no titanium, and the only stated compositional intervention is boron addition. Formation of TiB2 therefore lacks a stated Ti source and is incompatible with the proposed otherwise-identical base-to-boron-modified comparison.
